day4_after_start.text: *After school. The bell rang. The classroom empties out. Inside my bag, the envelope and the SD card case knock against each other.*

day4_after_start_2.text: *I write down the clues I saw at lunch.*

day4_after_start_3.text: *Sea heads for the student council room. Ms. Eunsu should be in the faculty office, and Nurse Riin in her office.*

choices: Follow Sea
Go see Ms. Eunsu
Confront Ms. Riin

day4_after_sea_route.text: *I followed Sea to the student council room.*

day4_after_sea_2.text:
*Sea closes the door behind me and locks it. The click echoes down the empty corridor.*

The reason I asked to see you alone after school is because there's something I need to check.

day4_after_sea_3.text: Alright. The door's locked, so let's talk the rest through in here.

day4_after_sea_4.text:
*Sea's eyes are red around the edges. A crumpled tissue lies on the desk.*

Have you been crying? If it's about me, just tell me.

day4_after_sea_5.text:
*Outside the window, students are leaving the sports field. Through the glass, their mouth movements and laughter are out of sync.*

See the students outside? Their mouths and laughter don’t match. Do you notice it too?

day4_after_sea_7.text:
*Sea won't look away.*

I'm right here. Talk to me instead of staring.

day4_after_sea_8.text: How many times has it been?

day4_after_sea_10.text:
How many times what? Don't cut yourself off.

*Sea's lips part twice before she barely gets the words out.*

day4_after_sea_force.text:
*'Forget it.' Even after saying that, Sea can't press her lips shut. Her fingertips keep fiddling with the knot of the bracelet on her wrist.*

Stop telling me to forget it. I can tell you're hiding something.
choices: I won't ask anymore
Tell me everything right now

day4_after_sea_accept.text: *Even after hearing that, Sea doesn't step aside from the locked door.*

day4_after_sea_accept_3.text:
*Sea looks out the window. The sunset paints the student council room in red.*

Can I leave once the sun sets?

day4_after_sea_confess_2.text: What do you mean, twelve times? Don't talk like I should know things I can't remember.

day4_after_sea_confess_3.text: I put your name tag on this desk twelve times. I heard you say "I'll come tomorrow too" twelve times.

day4_after_sea_confess_4.text: Every morning on the fifth day, you looked past my shoulder.

day4_after_sea_confess_5.text:
*Sea raised the cuff of her sleeve to rub the corner of her eye, then stopped her hand.*

So it wasn't your first time seeing me. I didn't know a thing—I really thought it was my first day.

day4_after_sea_confess_6.text: For the 9th time, you made me a bracelet. With ‘Sea’ engraved on the inside.

day4_after_sea_confess_7.text:
*Sea rolls up her uniform sleeve. The old string bracelet wrapped around her wrist is frayed in several spots.*

Can I look at it up close? I can't even recognize something I made with my own hands.

day4_after_sea_confess_8.text: The tenth time, you saw this and asked, 'It's pretty, who gave it to you?'

day4_after_sea_confess_9.text: You tied it for me. There wasn’t even a mark on your wrist.

day4_after_sea_confess_10.text:
*Sea smiles with wet eyes.*

This isn't funny. How can you smile when I've forgotten everything?

day4_after_sea_12loop.text:
*Sea grabs my arm tight.*

I'm not going anywhere. Just talk to me. Don't grab me like that.

day4_after_sea_12loop_2.text: *She murmurs, almost too quietly to hear.*

day4_after_sea_12loop_4.text: Seojin? What did you just call me? You know my name.

day4_after_sea_12loop_6.text:
*Sea’s grip tightens, wrinkling the sleeve of my uniform.*

Let go and answer me. I asked who that was.

day4_after_sea_12loop_7.text: *Seojin. It's not my name, yet the end of the syllables catches familiarly in my ear. The third name wedged into the previous records.*

day4_after_sea_12loop_9.text:
*She won’t let go of my arm. Her fingers keep crumpling my uniform sleeve.*

Then let go.

day4_after_sea_12loop_10.text: *On Sea's wrist as she clutches my sleeve, the old string bracelet from earlier flips over, exposing the small tab inside the knot.*

day4_after_sea_12loop_11.text:
*'Sea' written tiny on the inside. Even the habit of hooking the final stroke to the left is unmistakably my handwriting.*

The writing inside—it's really my exact handwriting. Right down to the way the end of the stroke bends.

day4_after_sea_12loop_12.text:
*Sea notices my gaze frozen on the inside of the bracelet, too.*

It's unmistakably my habit, yet the memory of braiding it is completely gone.

day4_after_sea_12loop_14.text:
*She's smiling. The moisture under her eyelashes still hasn't dried.*

Don't try to smile while you're crying.

day4_after_ft_sea_pre.text:
*Sea won't release my arm as I try to rise.*

I'm not running away. Let go of my arm.

day4_after_ft_sea.text: If you have something to say, say it. It won't change anything.

day4_after_ft_sea_choice.text: *What am I supposed to say? Sea's hand is still gripping my arm.*
choices: I'm sorry I forgot everything.
What did you remember through all twelve times?
I won't forget this time. Let's get out together.

day4_after_ft_sea_apologize.text: I've heard that thirteen times. I know you meant it every time.

day4_after_ft_sea_ask.text: I didn't remember. I wrote it down again every time.

day4_after_ft_sea_promise.text: I've heard that too. You said it, then forgot the next day.

day4_after_ft_sea_post.text:
*Sea finally let go. Marks from her fingers remained on my forearm. She tugged the cuff of her shirt down to cover the frayed knot of the bracelet.*

Covering it with your sleeve won't change that I already saw everything.

day4_after_eunsu_route.text: *I headed for the faculty office. The envelope in my bag taps against my side with every step.*

day4_after_eunsu_2.text:
*Ms. Eunsu sees me and sighs. She still looks tired. She is alone in the faculty office. All the chairs at the other desks are pushed neatly underneath.*

You're alone. Don't avoid me. Let's talk.

day4_after_eunsu_4.text: ...Have you seen what number you are on the attendance register?

day4_after_eunsu_4a.text:
*Even as she speaks, Ms. Eunsu pours hot water into the dripper. The stream from the kettle's spout flows without a tremor.*

I didn't come for a slot number—I came to see my records.

day4_after_eunsu_5.text:
*Once both cups were full, she set one down in front of me.*

You already know what I've noticed. Forget the coffee—let's talk about that first.

day4_after_eunsu_6.text:
*Two spoonfuls of sugar, half a measure of cream. The exact ratio I always mixed for myself at home.*

How do you know how I take my coffee? I haven't mentioned it once since coming to this school.

day4_after_eunsu_7.text: *It's not an item on any admission form, and I've never drunk coffee in the faculty office.*

day4_after_eunsu_8.text: That's right, isn't it? Your preference.

day4_after_eunsu_9.text:
*Ms. Eunsu smiles. The coffee cup’s handle points toward my left hand.*

Even the handle. Is coffee the only thing you've arranged for me?

day4_after_eunsu_10.text: *The desk drawer is half open. I can see Post-it notes inside. Dozens of them. Dense handwriting. -- All names. Different names. Some with lines crossed through them.*

day4_after_eunsu_11.text:
*On the bottom Post-it, my name. No line through it.*

Were those names transfer students too? Why hasn’t mine been crossed out?

day4_after_eunsu_13.text: It's okay, {name}. I'll put it back in order.

day4_after_eunsu_14.text:
*Ms. Eunsu’s hand stops above my head. The fingers that were about to stroke it curl inward.*

Don't touch me. First tell me what you mean by adjusting me again.

day4_after_eunsu_15.text:
*There is red pen ink on those fingertips. The same color as the check marks in the management ledger.*

There's red ink on your fingertips. That's from the pen you used to check the register, isn't it?

day4_after_riin_route.text: *I went to the nurse's office. The smell of disinfectant seeps out through the gap beneath the door.*

day4_after_riin_2.text:
*Nurse Riin is sorting papers. When she sees me, her hands stop and she turns the papers over. The movement looks natural, but I have already read the title: “S-13 Medication Records.”*

Don't turn it over. S-13. That's my medication record, isn't it?

day4_after_riin_3.text: What is it? Don't sneak up without a sound and startle me.

day4_after_riin_4.text:
*Her hand stays on the turned-over papers. Part of the title is still visible beneath her palm: `S-13`.*

I can see it even with your hand over it. If it's my record, let me read it.

day4_after_riin_6.text:
*Three seconds of silence pass. Ms. Riin doesn't take her eyes off my face.*

Don't just stare at me—please say something.

day4_after_riin_7.text: How much have you figured out?

day4_after_riin_8.text:
*Nurse Riin speaks calmly, then gets up, checks the nurse's office door and locks it.*

Why lock it? If I tell you what I saw, will you let me leave?

day4_after_riin_10.text: The logbook you just closed and M-13 inside the cabinet. Plus the names erased from the attendance book.

day4_after_riin_11.text:
*Ms. Riin doesn't open her mouth until the thermometer's indicator light goes out.*

I can't turn back pretending I don't know. Please tell me what you know.

day4_after_riin_12.text: ...That was fast. Faster than the twelfth.

day4_after_riin_15.text:
*She pulls a small metal key from her coat pocket.*

You're planning to give me that key, right? Tell me right now which door it opens.

day4_after_riin_16.text:
*Ms. Riin's hand hesitates in midair as she reaches toward me.*

Don't hesitate—just hand it over.

day4_after_riin_18.text:
*The key slips back into her coat pocket. Biting the corner of her lip, she murmurs something low about a 'cleanup schedule.'*

Don't just tell me not right now. What's going to change if I wait?

day4_after_riin_19.text: What's that cleanup schedule you just mentioned? You owe it to me to tell me what's going to happen to me.

day4_after_riin_21.text:
*Nurse Riin looks at me. Her crooked name-tag lanyard doesn’t move.*

Tomorrow's the last day. Should I come first thing in the morning?

day4_after_riin_22.text: Don't move tonight. And don't tell anyone about this.

day4_after_riin_24.text: *Ms. Riin's voice drops a register lower.*

day4_after_riin_25.text: I'll keep them out until tomorrow morning.

day4_after_riin_26.text:
*She turns her head away toward the sunset-drenched schoolyard. The infirmary floor flushes crimson.*

Don't look away—please look at me when you talk.

day4_after_end.text: *The sun sets, and the lights in the classroom windows go out one by one. Tomorrow is the fifth day.*

day4_xover_yuna_1.text:
*I paused as I stepped out the classroom door. Across the empty corner of the hallway, an afterimage of Yuna standing there yesterday flickers past.*

Yuna? Is it okay to talk out in the hallway? When you're the one stopping me first, it feels like something happened.

day4_xover_yuna_2.text: Sunbae, do you know the name Lee Junho?

day4_xover_yuna_5.text: It was like that every time in the records, too. Showing up with the same face, saying you don't know anything.

day4_xover_yuna_6.text: *In my memory, Yuna opens a thin print album and holds it out.*

day4_xover_yuna_7.text: They're all right here. From number one up to now.

day4_xover_yuna_8.text: Every single one of them is you, sunbae.

day4_xover_yuna_9.text:
*The twelve prints in the album held the same uniform, the same corridor, and the same face. Only the expression changed from photo to photo.*

I don't remember any of it. Only the face is mine. And you still spoke to me after seeing all this?

day4_xover_yuna_10.text: *When I blinked, the afterimage of Yuna closing the album scattered into the sunset at the end of the corridor.*

day4_xover_yuna_skip.text: *Stepping out of the classroom, I looked back toward the end of the hall. The corridor toward the photography club is empty.*

day4_xover_yuna_skip_met.text: *Stepping out of the classroom, I looked back toward the end of the hall. Only the spot by the window where Yuna stood yesterday lies empty.*

day4_xover_yuna_skip_2.text: No. Let's check somewhere else first.

day4_xover_yuna_skip_3.text: *I turned away. Only long stretches of evening sunlight lie across the empty hallway.*

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_menu.text: I chose a fact that hasn't been said yet. You can't even take out evidence that isn't in your hand.
choices: Put the photo on the table
Point to the keychain
I bring up the story of the nameless ampoule.
say no more now

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_0_1.text: I took out the printed photo Yuna had given me and set it on the table. The moment its front side came into view, Ms. Eunsu's hand froze over the file folder.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_0_3.text: Tell me who's in the photo first.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_0_4.text: The teacher did not touch the photo. Instead, she just rubbed the table with her fingertips to see if the corner was damp.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_0_5.text: If that's the original, don't fold it. We'll need it later when we check the date.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_0_6.text: Before she finished speaking, I slipped the photo into my pocket. The teacher swallowed her words asking for it back.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_1_1.text: The basement door opens with that key, right?

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_1_2.text: As the teacher put the string around her neck into her blouse, there was a sound of keys hitting each other.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_1_3.text: Tell me first which door you're talking about.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_1_4.text: If I tell you, you're going to change the lock.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_1_5.text: The pen on the table rolled out of the teacher’s hand. While I was picking it up, the key string came out again.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_1_6.text: That door opens from the inside. That's not something I can change.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_2_1.text: Why aren't the medicines in the nurse's office labeled?

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_2_2.text: The teacher looked at my left arm. Even though the sleeves were not rolled up, the gaze stopped at the elbow.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_2_3.text: Ask Ms. Riin about the medication.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_2_4.text: If you're the one who sent it, I should ask you.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_2_5.text: When the teacher closed the folder, only the tab with my name on it came out.

day4_after_eunsu_evidence_2_6.text: I'll check what you took. Until I've checked it, don't take anything anyone hands you.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_0.text: As soon as she closed her mouth, I spoke up first to press on.
choices: Write down what I heard in my notebook
Ask why the answer changed
End the conversation and step back

day4_after_eunsu_followup_0_write_1.text: When I pulled out my pen and wrote down her answer about the photo's date, she lowered her gaze to see which line I was filling in.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_0_write_2.text: I closed my notebook and slipped it into my pocket. If she tries to change her story later, she'll have to account for the line I just wrote first.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_0_press_1.text: What's said in the faculty office and what's written in a report aren't the same. Decide first which answer you want.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_0_press_2.text: She pushed the pen on her desk toward me. Without picking it up, I slid it back to the middle of the table.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_1.text: Once the key chain slipped out of sight beneath her collar, I spoke again.
choices: Write down what I heard in my notebook
Ask why the answer changed
End the conversation and step back

day4_after_eunsu_followup_1_write_1.text: As I copied into my notebook that the door opened from the inside, she quietly looked down at the line I had written.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_1_write_2.text: I clicked the ballpoint pen shut and put away my notebook. Now that I've heard how the basement door works, she'll have to explain this note first if she changes her tune later.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_1_press_1.text: Answering by the safety rules and tipping you off privately aren't the same. If you want to ask everything, watch the clock while you do it.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_1_press_2.text: Her fingertip tapped the corner of the file folder once. I met her gaze without looking away.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_2.text: Catching the pause as her hand stilled on the folder tab, I asked again.
choices: Write down what I heard in my notebook
Ask why the answer changed
End the conversation and step back

day4_after_eunsu_followup_2_write_1.text: While I wrote down her promise to check the infirmary medication, she leaned in slightly to read my handwriting.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_2_write_2.text: I folded my notebook shut and pocketed it. I'll need this record to cross-check whether the infirmary or the faculty office changes its story.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_2_press_1.text: What I tell you as your homeroom teacher and what I leave behind in charge of records aren't the same. Leave it at that for today.

day4_after_eunsu_followup_2_press_2.text: She pushed the cooling cup of coffee aside. I didn't touch mine either.

day4_after_sea_evidence_menu.text: I chose a fact that hasn't been said yet. You can't even take out evidence that isn't in your hand.
choices: Show a photo of the rooftop engraving
Ask about the history of force quitting the app.
say no more now

day4_after_sea_evidence_0_1.text: When I turned on the engraved photo under the wire mesh, Sea tried to snatch my phone. First, I turned off the screen.

day4_after_sea_evidence_0_2.text: Did you go to the rooftop? I told you not to touch the railing there.

day4_after_sea_evidence_0_3.text: Do you know who engraved it?

day4_after_sea_evidence_0_4.text: Sea hid her left hand behind her back and rubbed the ring mark on her finger with her thumb.

day4_after_sea_evidence_0_5.text: Where did you see that name? There wasn't a name in the photo.

day4_after_sea_evidence_0_6.text: Sea also noticed that I hadn't said Seolhwa yet. The chair was pushed back a little.

day4_after_sea_evidence_1_1.text: Did you get an alert when I shut down the app on the first day too?

day4_after_sea_evidence_1_2.text: Sea nodded right away, then pressed her lips shut when she realized she had answered too quickly.

day4_after_sea_evidence_1_3.text: I thought the battery was dead. So I checked.

day4_after_sea_evidence_1_4.text: I only closed the app. What's that got to do with the battery?

day4_after_sea_evidence_1_5.text: The cell phone rang once in Sea's hand. Sea stopped vibrating without seeing the notification.

day4_after_sea_evidence_1_6.text: When you turn it off, they question me too. They ask why I didn't stop you. I have to answer them.

day4_after_sea_followup_0.text: When Sea bit her lip and trailed off, I pressed her first this time.
choices: Write down what I heard in my notebook
Ask why the answer changed
End the conversation and step back

day4_after_sea_followup_0_write_1.text: As I jotted down what she'd said about the rooftop railing in my notebook, Sea ducked her head to see which line I was writing.

day4_after_sea_followup_0_write_2.text: I closed my notebook and tucked it into my pocket. If anyone tries to change their story later, they'll have to explain the line I just wrote first.

day4_after_sea_followup_0_press_1.text: Back then I had no choice but to brush it off like that. It's not like I'm the only one keeping stories straight around you.

day4_after_sea_followup_0_press_2.text: Sea glanced toward the student council room door. Outside the frosted glass, someone's shadow stood motionless.

day4_after_sea_followup_1.text: I spoke again to Sea as she stared down at the phone after its vibration died.
choices: Write down what I heard in my notebook
Ask why the answer changed
End the conversation and step back

day4_after_sea_followup_1_write_1.text: I wrote down that app-shutdown alerts went to Sea as well. Sea's eyes nervously followed the tip of my pen.

day4_after_sea_followup_1_write_2.text: I folded the notebook into my pocket. If she tries to play dumb even about the guardian alerts, she'll have to explain this note first.

day4_after_sea_followup_1_press_1.text: I couldn't tell you the truth right from the start. I had to report back just as I was told, too.

day4_after_sea_followup_1_press_2.text: The shadow cast across the hallway windowpane slowly moved off. Sea didn't open her mouth until the footsteps faded away.
